bh.src: djok_bh_iw1 58.93 s (f1413): Essential Tennis "Djokovic Backhand in Super Slow Motion - BNP Paribas Open 2013" practice, court level, player whole and large (~1000 px); every frame of the 23.976 fps upload a distinct picture (no repeats: every frame used); slow factor 10x: the fall of the incoming ball in this video (iw1 23.1-24.3 s) fitted with its own shrinking size as the scale gives 9.3x (9.8x if its blurred edge inflates its size 10%), a ball in djok_bh_iw3 gives 11.4-12.7x - spin moves both (topspin low, slice high), so 10x (a 240 fps camera conformed to 24 fps) is taken, +-15%; same camera as bh_set1 (psi 220). From above the grip at contact is out to his left, level with the left foot and 0.1 m behind the hips toward the net (he lunges to his left and slightly back; seen from the camera the hands are in front of his body) - not a grip placed behind the body. One camera in front-left: depth along its line is the pose model's guess; the camera follows the run, so travel across the picture comes from the tracker's background match and is approximate; feet below the picture edge in the first 0.15 s; spurious camera-tilt reading zeroed; toes float up to ~0.1 m. fh.src: nadal_fb_2 (Essential Tennis, Nadal 2013 Cincinnati practice, 1080p 23.976 fps) 64.6-79.2 s, contact 69.65 s (f1670, ball on the strings); court level at his RIGHT side, a little behind him (his back to the camera in the take-back), camera panning to follow; psi 90 set from the court: the baseline beside him recedes straight into the picture with the centre-mark tick pointing right, so the net is to the right of the picture; slow factor 9.4x: this shoot's measured ball-toss free fall (9.0-9.7x), and my own gravity fit to the incoming ball's arc in the same video's 88 s backhand gives 9.35x (8.8-10.1x; no spin assumed); every frame a distinct picture (no repeats or made-up frames: 225 pictures per real second), all used; the shot starts after a dissolve at 64.5 s, so the clip begins 0.52 s before contact with the racket already up
fh.why: checked at 8 phases against the frames (side row = this camera): very wide open stance with the racket up and back and the right hand near the throat, left arm straight back at shoulder height, racket dropped low behind him, contact in front of the right (front) leg at hip height with the free right arm folded in front of the chest (in front, not behind), finish wrapped high over the head, hips turning toward his right and the right foot stepping back behind the left - all match; from above: hand behind at the drop, forward-left at contact. Travel checked against the baseline in the picture (not just the background pan): the left foot steps back wide, the right foot drags back ~0.5 m and the hips move ~1 m away from the net before contact. The hitting (left) arm is hidden behind his back from -0.06 to -0.02 s and from +0.01 to +0.05 s (tracker visibility 0.01-0.2): there the tracker's wrist jumped 0.6 m in one frame and stalled, so the left wrist/hand picture positions were in-betweened from the frames where they are seen (and the left elbow +0.01..+0.05 s), checked against the frames (racket handle position); wrist peak 10.1 m/s at -0.07 s after that (the shipped Nadal forehand: 11.3). Camera at his side: across-court depth (of the arms, and how far the hips turn past side-on: -112 deg at -0.52 s) is set from bone lengths, the stroke's rules and the pose model; few foot-down flags; a one-frame wrist flick at +0.46 s in the recovery (14.5 m/s for one 60th, then back), not repaired

bh.src: nadal_fb_2 (Essential Tennis, Nadal 2013 Cincinnati practice, 1080p 23.976 fps) 79.8-95.2 s, contact 87.98 s (the ball reverses between f2109 and f2110); court level IN FRONT of him, about 30 deg toward his right side, whole body ~1000 px, camera panning to follow; psi 150 from his hips and shoulders square in the ready position (148-154 in the camera's frame), the tracker's face estimate (159) and the incoming ball (crossing the picture to the left while shrinking ~8%, i.e. also travelling away from the camera); slow factor 9.4x: this shoot's measured ball-toss free fall (9.0-9.7x), and my gravity fit to this ball's arc gives 9.35x (8.8-10.1x; no spin assumed); every frame a distinct picture (225 per real second), all used; shot runs from a dissolve at 79.6 s to the fade at 95.3 s
bh.why: checked at 8 phases against the frames (front row is closest to this camera): racket held out front with both hands as he moves to his right, racket taken back low on his right with both hands in a wide stance (shoulders turned ~55 deg, hips ~20), contact in front of the body at waist height with both hands together on the grip and IN FRONT of him (0.2 m ahead of the pelvis; not behind), finish high over the left shoulder wrapping behind the head, then a wide crouched recovery - all match. Both wrists seen by the tracker through contact (vis 0.95); after +0.05 s the left (top) hand is hidden and is put on the grip by the two-hander rule. The tracker's camera-pan estimate misfired on five frames (f2089-2090, f2115-2116: 30-105 px jumps against ~3 px; f2221 vertical) and was replaced by its neighbours' median, which removed a 0.35 m one-frame jump in travel at +0.05 s. Camera in front: toward-the-net depth (and travel along it) is the model's/rules' estimate; hitting wrist peak 7.1 m/s across and up (the forward swing is mostly depth here); few foot-down flags
bh.situationWhy: neutral rally backhand: moves ~1 m to his right at ~1.1 m/s while taking the racket back, sets a wide semi-open stance and meets the ball at waist height (wrist 1.18 m) in front; recovers to a wide crouch
